page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1ne.8xlarge is a storage-dense instance powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor operating at 2.5 GHz on an x86_64 architecture. Managed via KVM virtualization, the server features 32 dedicated vCPUs paired with 128.0 GB of RAM, offering 4.0 GB of system memory per vCPU core. Network infrastructure delivers a baseline bandwidth rate of 20 Gbps.

The primary feature of the ecs.d1ne.8xlarge instance is its massive local storage array, comprising 94,489 GB of local HDD capacity. Unlike NVMe-based storage configurations built for high random IOPS, this local mechanical hard drive volume focuses on offering high capacity per resource unit. This design presents a distinct performance tradeoff: while it supplies broad sequential throughput and exceptional capacity for bulk data retention, random read and write latency is inherently constrained compared to solid-state solutions.

From a cost efficiency perspective, bundling large local HDD volumes with balanced compute resources offers a favorable capacity-to-cost ratio for bulk logging, cold data storage, distributed file systems, and mass media archives. The combination of 32 dedicated vCPUs, 20 Gbps network bandwidth, and 128 GB RAM supports processing large datasets locally without incurring network storage transfer overhead, provided the access patterns prioritize sequential disk I/O.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1ne.8xlarge is a high-density local storage instance powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 CPU on the x86_64 architecture. Managed using KVM virtualization, it provides 32 dedicated vCPUs and 128.0 GB of memory, resulting in a ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The server includes 94,489 GB of local HDD storage and supports a baseline network bandwidth of 20 Gbps without GPU hardware. The vast HDD capacity offers high raw storage density at a low cost per gigabyte relative to SSD configurations. However, mechanical storage trades away low random access latency in favor of sequential throughput and sheer volume. The ecs.d1ne.8xlarge is well-matched for big data processing frameworks like Apache Hadoop, distributed logging clusters, backup repositories, and long-term data archival systems requiring direct-attached mechanical disk capacity.
